title: Bronze lamp with a Silenus-head lid and two dolphins, found at Pong Tuek in Kanchanaburi — the Bangkok National Museum calls it a Roman lantern
language_note:
The Fine Arts Department's own English, on the English-language side of its virtual-museum site. It is not a native-speaker English and it is not repaired — `the god of Roman`, `two dolphins were collision facing`, `The district still located on the trade routes`. A curator who tidied that prose would be substituting his own words for the museum's in the one field the loader chunks, which is the rule `africa-07-cosmas-sasu` set for an 1897 edition's four-hyphen dashes and applies here to a translation the institution made of its own catalog.

THE MUSEUM DATES THE OBJECT IN THE BUDDHIST ERA AND THIS CORPUS DOES NOT CONVERT IT. `about last 6th Buddhist century` and `approximately 9-10 Buddhist century` are the two datings the record offers, in พุทธศตวรรษ, and converting them into CE centuries here would be this project authoring a date the way `NEVER AUTHOR A COORDINATE` forbids it authoring a point. The `date` field carries what the museum printed.
date: NOT STATED. The record's `ERA AGE :` field is printed as `...` — the museum's own placeholder, left empty. The only dating anywhere on the page is inside the description, and it is two datings rather than one: `about last 6th Buddhist century` OR `approximately 9-10 Buddhist century`, which are several hundred years apart. Both are in the Buddhist era and neither is converted here.
findspot: `Found from Pong Tuek sub district, Tar Ma Ka district, Kanchanaburi Province.` — the museum's own words, a three-level Thai administrative address. The object is in the `Bangkok National Museum, Room of Asia arts, Mahasurasinghanat Building`. NO ACCESSION NUMBER IS PRINTED ANYWHERE ON THE RECORD, which is why `museum_number` is absent from this file; the museum publishes a highlight page for this object and not a catalog entry.

findspot_places.name: Pong Tuek, Tha Maka district, Kanchanaburi Province, Thailand
findspot_places.note:
`regional` AND NOT `stated`, THOUGH THE SOURCE STATES THE PLACE EXACTLY. The rule in this repository is that `ground: "stated"` on a specific place requires a gazetteer id, and without one the honest ground is `regional`. Pleiades is a Greco-Roman gazetteer and does not reach central Thailand — the 2026-08-12 survey found no Pleiades entry for Óc Eo, Khao Sam Kaeo or Gyeongju either, which is Mundus Ulterior's own premise showing up in its gate. GeoNames is this corpus's second gazetteer and covers modern Thailand, but no GeoNames dump for Thailand is held in `data/`, and nothing enters this corpus on a remembered id.

SO THIS IS A COORDINATE THE SOURCE HANDED OVER AND THE CORPUS REFUSED, and it is the third of them: the two Scandinavian placements in the debt list are the others. **A Thai GeoNames dump would close it, exactly as the Swedish dump would close those.** Named here so the debt is one line of work with a name on it rather than a shrug.

origin_places.name: Alexandria under Roman rule — where the museum suggests the lamp was made
origin_places.note: NO ID, AND THE REASON IS THE MUSEUM'S OWN HEDGE. The description reads `This lamp may be wrought in Alexandria, Egypt when under Roman rule`. Pleiades holds Alexandria, and importing its id would convert a `may be` into a point on a map — the same move `NEVER AUTHOR A COORDINATE` forbids, one step further back. `regional` records that the museum places the object's manufacture in the Roman Mediterranean without the corpus asserting the city. `africa-07-cosmas-sasu` treats Sasu the same way, for the same reason in the other direction: there the source places somewhere only by relation, here it places it only by conjecture.

original_text_excerpt:
Lantern with lid molded to face of Silenus, the god of Roman. Handle was palm leaf and two dolphins  were collision facing. This lamp may be wrought in Alexandria, Egypt when under Roman rule as about last 6th Buddhist century or century wrought approximately 9-10 Buddhist century and the Indian traders brought into the country. The district still located on the trade routes of the Indian traders once traveled by.
Found from Pong Tuek sub district, Tar Ma Ka district, Kanchanaburi Province.
original_text_note:
TWO FIELDS FROM THE MUSEUM'S HIGHLIGHT RECORD, IN A DECLARED ORDER: the whole of `FEATURE :`, then the whole of `HISTORY :`, joined by a single newline. The field labels are not carried and nothing else is added.

VERIFIED BY DIGEST ACROSS TWO MACHINES, AND THE DIGEST CAUGHT AN ERROR ON THE FIRST ATTEMPT. There is exactly one non-ASCII character in these 495 — a NON-BREAKING SPACE at index 99, between `dolphins` and the ordinary space before `were`. The first transcription on the bridge put the ordinary space first and the U+00A0 second, which is invisible in every rendering of the text and changes the digest completely. The two machines disagreed, the byte order was read off the browser as a code-point list, and the transcription was corrected.

    chars 495   sha256 9593d792b77de010a267b4222c3f47d84e70eaa745e2c41697bdae7e3a6dfd2e

THAT IS THE THIRD TIME THIS PRACTICE HAS EARNED ITS KEEP AND THE FIRST TIME IT HAS CAUGHT A CURATOR RATHER THAN A PAGE. On `arabia-07-cih541` the digest revealed forty-four non-breaking spaces in a line-number gutter that no reader would have seen; on `eastasia-08-songshi-fulin` it verified an edit rather than a paste. Here both machines were transcribing the same visible characters and one of them got the ORDER of two invisible ones wrong. No amount of reading the two texts side by side would have found it.

THE PAGE IS SERVED OVER HTTP AND THAT COST A STEP. `crypto.subtle` is unavailable outside a secure context, so the browser-side digest could not use the Web Crypto API; SHA-256 was implemented in the page and checked against the known digest of `abc` before it was used on anything.

citation_original:
THE SOURCE STATES NO TERMS, AND UNDER RULING 74 THAT IS USABLE AND THE RECORD MUST SAY SO IN THOSE WORDS. **THE SOURCE STATES NO TERMS.**

The position is `states_no_terms` and this is THE FIRST RECORD IN THIS CORPUS TO USE IT — see FINDING 88, because `F7_START.md` says all seven positions had been exercised and six had.

No quotation is carried, because the position may not carry one: there is nothing to quote. What was looked at, on 2026-09-06: the object page itself, the site's `About us` page, and the site's footer on both. The only copyright line anywhere on either page is `© 2009-2014 by GPIUTMD`, which appears beneath a Joomla login block and names a TEMPLATE VENDOR. It is a credit for the site's design and it is not the Fine Arts Department saying anything about the reuse of its catalogue text. No terms-of-use page, no permissions page, no licence, and no reuse statement was found; the navigation offers `About us`, `Service`, `Organization` and `Contact us` and nothing else.

WHY NOT `all_rights_reserved`. That position asserts what a source SAID and must quote it verbatim, and the only quotable line would be the template vendor's credit. Recording `© 2009-2014 by GPIUTMD` as the Bangkok National Museum's rights position would attribute a third party's copyright notice to the museum, which is a claim about the source that the source does not make. FINDING 69 exists because two licence claims went wrong in opposite directions in a single session; this is the direction where a curator invents a restriction rather than a permission, and it is no better.

THE SEARCH BOUNDARY. Only the English-language side of the site was read. The Thai-language pages were not opened and no negative is recorded against them; a terms statement may exist there.
notes:
F7's first Southeast Asia `catalogue_record` slot. Fourth record of the tranche, fifty-first in the corpus.

THE MOST FAMOUS MEDITERRANEAN OBJECT FOUND IN THAILAND, AND THE MUSEUM THAT HOLDS IT CALLS IT A ROMAN LANTERN IN ITS OWN TITLE. A cast bronze lamp with its lid moulded as the head of Silenus, a palm-leaf handle and two dolphins facing each other, found at Pong Tuek in Kanchanaburi and displayed in Bangkok. The museum's own account of how it got there is the sentence this record exists for: made in Alexandria under Roman rule, and `the Indian traders brought into the country`, along a route the district still sits on.

WHAT SOUTHEAST ASIA DID NOT HAVE. The corpus's Southeast Asian records are the Óc Eo Antoninus medallion, an Óc Eo site summary, a Khao Sam Kaeo intaglio, and four inscriptions in local languages. Every object among them is small and portable — a coin, a medallion, a carved gem. This is a piece of Mediterranean FURNITURE, twenty-seven centimetres of cast bronze, and the difference matters: an intaglio can arrive in a purse, and a lamp arrives as freight.

AND THE ROUTE IS THE MUSEUM'S ARGUMENT, NOT OURS. The record does not say the lamp came from Rome to Thailand; it says it was made in Roman Egypt and carried by INDIAN traders. That is the shape the corpus's South Asian records describe from the other end — `southasia-02-periplus-muziris` and `southasia-03-muziris-papyrus` document Roman cargo reaching Indian ports, and this is a Roman object continuing east from there in Indian hands. The two ends of one route, held by two regions of this corpus, and neither record cites the other.

NOT DECLARED GLOSS-CAPABLE, AND IT IS THE THIRD F7 RECORD OF WHICH THAT IS TRUE. The description hedges twice inside the chunked field — `This lamp may be wrought in Alexandria` and two datings several centuries apart, `about last 6th Buddhist century or century wrought approximately 9-10 Buddhist century`. Mechanically that is a hedged identification with a statement of uncertainty attached. F7 holds ONE declaration, it is Block F's last, and it is spent on `persia-07-met-ewer-anahita`. Recorded here, as on `arabia-08-walters-marib-pediment`, so a later block can see the material without re-reading the record to find it.

A NEGATIVE RECORDED BY A FETCHER IS NOT A NEGATIVE ABOUT A SOURCE. The search pass could not open this page: the host serves an HTTPS-to-HTTP redirect that a fetcher's mandatory upgrade turns into a loop, and it recorded the URL as unverified. It opens in a browser on the first attempt. `betamasaheft.eu`'s 403 and `collections.louvre.fr`'s bot challenge are negatives recorded BY A BROWSER and stand differently.

NO ACCESSION NUMBER AND NO DATE, AND BOTH ARE THE MUSEUM'S SILENCE RATHER THAN THIS RECORD'S. `museum_number` is absent because the page prints none; `date` carries the museum's `...` and its two Buddhist-era centuries because that is all it prints. A catalogue record with no catalogue number is a weaker record than `southasia-07-bm-claudius-aureus`, and the weakness is stated rather than papered over.
